contentHtml:
UAE—Oris Dental Center has launched a home dental care service across Dubai to improve access to essential dental examinations and treatments for patients who face difficulties travelling to clinics.

The service targets families, particularly older adults, children and people with mobility limitations or health conditions that make clinic visits challenging.

The initiative also aligns with the UAE’s Year of the Family, which promotes family wellbeing and access to healthcare for all generations.

Patients can arrange home visits following an initial assessment to establish whether their dental needs can be addressed safely outside a clinical setting.

Dr Hussein Al Saleh, founder of Oris Dental Center and specialist prosthodontist and oral implantologist, said accessible healthcare was an important part of supporting family wellbeing.

“Making healthcare more accessible, regardless of age or mobility, is an important part of supporting healthier families and improving quality of life,” he said.

He noted that oral health extends beyond preventing tooth decay and gum disease, as it is also associated with overall health.

Research has linked periodontal disease with certain chronic conditions, including cardiovascular disease, highlighting the importance of regular dental examinations and appropriate follow-up care.

Home-based dental services and clinical safety

The service covers general dental examinations and oral health assessments, teeth cleaning, scaling and tartar removal, dental fillings, and evaluations of dental pain.

However, dentists will first assess each patient’s condition to determine which procedures can be performed safely at home.

Patients requiring specialised equipment, advanced diagnostic examinations or complex dental procedures will be referred to the dental center for further treatment.

Each home visit will involve a dentist and an assisting nurse equipped with portable dental instruments, sterile materials and other necessary supplies.

The team will follow established hygiene and infection-control protocols, while ensuring that treatment remains within the clinical limits of a home setting.

Al Saleh said patients have different dental needs depending on their age, health and mobility.

He added that home-based examinations and treatments could reduce the practical challenges families face when arranging dental appointments, although clinical assessments remain essential when determining appropriate treatment.

Oral health also affects everyday activities such as eating, chewing and speaking.

Dental pain and gum problems can disrupt nutrition, sleep and daily routines.

Early detection of tooth decay and gum inflammation allows dentists to intervene before these conditions develop into more complex problems.

Availability across Dubai

The service is available across Dubai seven days a week by prior appointment.

Patients or their family members can contact Oris Dental Center, provide information about their symptoms and medical condition, and arrange an assessment with the clinical team.

Requests involving urgent dental concerns will be evaluated according to clinical needs and team availability.

The center also advises patients to brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste, clean between their teeth regularly, reduce sugar consumption and attend routine dental examinations according to their individual needs.

Children and older adults may require closer monitoring because their oral healthcare needs change with age and health status.

The introduction of home-based dental services reflects a broader shift towards patient-centred healthcare delivery, in which providers extend selected clinical services beyond traditional facilities.

For dental providers, this model requires investment in portable equipment, trained personnel, infection-control procedures and clear referral pathways to ensure continuity of care.
